title: [ORION-QG QG-35] Summary-conditioned fixed probe complexity: fair baseline for adaptive identification
body:
Parent programme: #740.
Direct earned parents: QG-32 #911 (joint summary + universal 5-probe upper bound), QG-32c #928 (exact universal fixed minimum 5).
Pending comparison target: QG-34 #924 (exact adaptive minimax depth; outcome intentionally unknown at freeze).

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE FAIR-BASELINE LANE. FREEZE BEFORE ANY QG-34 ADAPTIVE DEPTH OUTCOME AND BEFORE ANY QG-35 CLASS-CONDITIONED FIXED-MINIMUM OUTCOME.**

QG-32c proves minimum 5 for a **single universal fixed probe set** that works across all 92 known joint bulk+spectrum summary classes. But QG-34's adaptive policy is allowed to know the initial joint summary class before choosing its first probe. A fair nonadaptive comparator must receive the same side information.

QG-35 therefore asks, for each initial joint class `S`:

> What is the minimum number `F(S)` of indexed probes, chosen after `S` is known but fixed before any probe outcomes are seen, whose joint response signature separates every orbit in `S`?

Define `F_* = max_S F(S)`.

No value of `F(S)` or `F_*` is predicted.

## Q1 — exact per-class fixed set-cover problem

For each of the 92 joint classes:
- universe = unordered orbit pairs inside the class;
- probe `p` covers a pair iff the two orbits have different exact `K[o,p]` response;
- `F(S)` is the minimum number of probes covering every pair in that class.

Singleton classes have `F(S)=0`.

## Q2 — production exact solver

Production must independently reconstruct the response matrix and solve each class exactly using bounded branch-and-bound / depth search for cardinalities 0..4, with the earned universal five-probe set as a constructive `<=5` fallback only.

Allowed sound reductions: identical coverage collapse, coverage dominance, uncovered-pair branching, max-cover cardinality lower bound, memoization.

Serialize:
- all 92 `F(S)` values;
- class-size / minimum histograms;
- `F_*` and worst classes;
- canonical minimum witness probe set for every worst class;
- exact verification that each witness separates its class.

## Q3 — independent verification

Generic ORION must use a distinct exact formulation/state encoding. Preferred: complete 0/1/2-half-union meet-in-the-middle for `<=4` where possible, then direct exact witness verification; if a class requires 5, independently prove no <=4 cover and bind the universal five-probe upper bound.

Native ORION-Q authorizes only summary-conditioned nonadaptive observation complexity on the frozen 715-orbit / 92-class problem.

Workflow requires deterministic replay and self-consistent class-minimum/witness tamper rejection.

## Q4 — fair adaptivity comparison (only after QG-34 is independently GREEN)

Do **not** compare QG-34 adaptive depth directly to QG-32c universal fixed minimum 5.

The fair comparison is:
- class-conditioned nonadaptive worst case: `F_*`;
- class-conditioned adaptive worst case: `D_*` from QG-34.

Only if both receipts are exact and `D_* < F_*` may a later composition authorize:
`TARE_POSTSUMMARY_ADAPTIVITY_STRICTLY_REDUCES_WORST_CASE_OBSERVATION_COUNT`.

If `D_* == F_*`, record no strict adaptivity advantage. If either receipt is not exact, CANNOT_CHECK.

## Hard boundaries

Always false:
- hardware/measurement minimum;
- full finite-n optimum;
- generic adaptive-testing novelty;
- physical quantum advantage;
- claims about compilation cost itself rather than observation/identification count.

## Donor subtraction

Set cover and decision-tree comparisons are donor methods. Candidate value is the exact compiler-specific, side-information-matched fixed-vs-adaptive observation complexity.

nodes.body:
QG-35 protected run 1 is **not accepted**. Production/generic differed on exactly one class: canonical joint class index 5, where production returned `F(5)=3` and independent MITM returned `F(5)=2`; all other 91 class minima and `F_*` agreed.

Root cause is a production search-method bug, not a scientific target change: the DFS combined uncovered-pair branching with a monotone `start` probe-index restriction. That restriction is unsound because a solution can contain a lower-index probe that does not cover the current pivot plus a higher-index probe that does; branching first on the pivot-covering higher-index probe then incorrectly makes the lower-index probe unavailable. The independent verifier exposed this counterexample.

Before rerun, production will remove only the `start` restriction and memoize exact feasibility by `(remaining_pairs, slots)`; already-selected probes cannot recur because their full coverage has been removed from `remaining_pairs`. The QG-35 scientific definition, domain, 0..5 cardinality ladder, five-probe upper-bound fallback, generic MITM verifier, native scope, replay/tamper gates, and QG-36 fair-comparison decision table are unchanged. Run 1 remains unearned.

**Retraction notice (now on main via #926).** The headline this issue builds on is null-reproducible: the separation counts (`85/92`, `708/715`, `D_*=3 < F_*=4 < U_*=5`, the regret curve) are reproduced by a row-shuffle null, and `85 = 92−7` / `708 = 715−7` are identities forced by the class-size histogram frozen before any solver ran. See `development/orion-qg-regime-geometry/QG_RETRACTION_SELECTION_HEADLINES_V1.md` and `QG_ADVERSARIAL_REFEREE_REPORT.md`. What survives: C1(b) descriptor completeness (whose ceiling theorem is Lehmann 1959 per the lane's own prior-art audit), witness disjointness, and the depth-3 residual (16 classes / 168 masks vs null-A mean 8.9 / 384 — noting null B in the residual script is uninformative by construction, being exactly permutation-invariant). Work on this issue should either retarget the surviving residual or close as superseded.
